facts.raw_span: a one-month history of burning sensation and discomfort in her left breast
without fever or systemic symptoms
a 3 × 3 cm palpable mass in the upper quadrant of the left breast
without overlying skin changes
No axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy was noted
Routine blood tests, chest radiograph, and ECG were unremarkable
Breast MRI revealed an ill-defined, deep retroareolar spiculated lesion measuring 3 × 1.5 cm
with an early enhancement peak and associated architectural distortion
no axillary lymphadenopathy or skin thickening was identified
BIRADS IV
breast tissue containing cohesive nests of neoplastic epithelial cells within a dense lymphoid infiltrate
the epithelial cells were positive for cytokeratin AE1/E3 and negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu

rationales.F01: Burning sensation and discomfort in the breast is a non-specific symptom.
rationales.F02: Absence of fever or systemic symptoms makes inflammatory breast cancer less likely.
rationales.F03: A palpable mass in the breast is a common finding in various breast cancers.
rationales.F04: Absence of overlying skin changes makes inflammatory breast cancer less likely.
rationales.F05: No axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy reduces the likelihood of advanced cancer.
rationales.F07: Breast MRI findings are consistent with a malignant lesion.
rationales.F08: Early enhancement peak and architectural distortion are suspicious for malignancy.
rationales.F10: BIRADS IV indicates a suspicious lesion that requires biopsy.
rationales.F11: Neoplastic epithelial cells within a dense lymphoid infiltrate are consistent with medullary carcinoma.
rationales.F12: Triple-negative breast cancer is suggested by the absence of estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu expression.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a dense lymphoid infiltrate and the epithelial cells being positive for cytokeratin AE1/E3 and negative for estrogen receptor, progesterone receptor, and HER2/neu support Medullary Carcinoma of the Breast, which is a subtype of triple-negative breast cancer.
